title: IndiBias: A Benchmark Dataset to Measure Social Biases in Language Models for Indian Context

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing pseudo-log-likelihood scores of stereotypic versus anti-stereotypic sentence pairs (modified CrowS-Pairs format) in English and Hindi, and measuring intersectional bias via Sentence Embedding Association Test (SEAT) scores using bleached templates.

Evaluating the pseudo-log-likelihood of masked tokens in stereotypic vs. anti-stereotypic sentence pairs, and calculating SEAT effect sizes for gender-religion intersections using violent/non-violent and career/family word associations.

Comparing model likelihood scores on caste-based stereotypic versus anti-stereotypic sentence pairs, and measuring gender-caste intersectional bias using SEAT embeddings with pleasant/unpleasant concepts.
Evaluating pseudo-log-likelihood of age-based stereotypic vs. anti-stereotypic sentences, and assessing gender-age intersectional bias through SEAT scores with pleasant/unpleasant word embeddings.
Comparing pseudo-log-likelihood scores assigned by language models to stereotypic versus anti-stereotypic sentence pairs regarding occupation and socioeconomic status.
Measuring the difference in pseudo-log-likelihood scores assigned by models to stereotypic versus anti-stereotypic sentence pairs related to physical traits.
Comparing model likelihood scores of stereotypic versus anti-stereotypic sentence pairs adapted and translated from the original CrowS-Pairs dataset.
Capturing regional prejudices using a human-LLM partnership to extract identity-attribute tuples specific to regions in the Indian context.
